proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity or power of an obligation to bind, direct, or compel action. It is internally grounded in the obligation-bearing entity (the bearer of the obligation role) and is a disposition because it is a realizable entity that grounds why the obligation has prescriptive pull — it can be realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or acknowledgment. It is not a quality (no scalar magnitude), not a role (not externally grounded by social context alone), but a disposition: a structural feature of the obligation that grounds its directiveness. BFO_0000016 (Disposition) is the best fit.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016): it is a realizable specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (the entity bound by the obligation) and is grounded in the nature of that binding relation, capable of being realized in processes of compliance or enforcement.
As a Disposition, NormativeForce is also a specifically dependent continuant (BFO_0000020), inhering in exactly one bearer — the agent or entity upon whom the obligation is incumbent.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce be modeled as a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation or related to it via a property (e.g., every LegalObligation bearer-of some NormativeForce)?

Is the normative force in question specifically legal (inhering in the bearer of a LegalObligation role) or more general (covering moral obligations as well)? This affects whether the bearer is restricted to legal persons.
Do you want to distinguish 'normative force' as the disposition from 'being bound' as the quality, or treat them as co-extensive here?
Should 'realized in' point to compliance processes (BehavioralLegalManifestation) or enforcement processes, or both?
proposal.rationale_summary: The normative force of an obligation is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016). A disposition in BFO is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer and is grounded in the bearer's own nature or structure — it does not require external grounding (which would make it a Role) and is not a measurable magnitude (which would make it a Quality). Normative force fits this profile: it is the intrinsic prescriptive pull or bindingness that inheres in the agent who bears the obligation, grounding their tendency to comply and capable of being realized in processes of compliance, acknowledgment, or enforcement (BFO_0000054 realized in). A new class 'NormativeForce' is proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000016. No existing working-ontology class precisely captures this concept, though it is closely related to the existing working:LegalObligation (BFO_0000023/Role) — the normative force would inhere in the bearer of a LegalObligation role, not in the role itself.
